### 🐛 Describe the bug

With `cudagraph_mode=FULL` and the FlashInfer sparse MLA backend on SM100 (`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`), the engine crashes as soon as a prefill chunk replays a FULL CUDA graph. `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, the default, works.

items.title: [ROCm] Support unlimited sequence lengths via multi-pass reduction
items.bodyExcerpt:
At present, on ROCm for certain models including GLM-4.7, vLLM has a choice between two attention implementations from vllm/v1/attention/ops/chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py. One is a very slow reference Triton kernel and the other is a  hand-coded op. The custom op only supports context length up to 131072 tokens, which means that, unless vLLM is set to eager mode, it'll only be used if max_seq_len is <131072 (otherwise, since actual context length is unknown at graph capture time, it defaults to Triton for all context lengths).

This patch drops the 131072 token cap and adds a multi-pass mode to support  unlimited max_seq_len. It also adds unit tests to cover this scenario.

This results in a drastic increase in token generation throughput on ROCm for GLM-4.7 for max_seq_len>131072.

Throughput, token/s, 4x MI325x (2026/Sep/09)
Context | max_model_len | PR - throughput | Baseline - throughput
-- | -- | -- | --
65536 | 75536 | 55.05 | 55.08
100000 | 110000 | 50.21 | 50.09
150000 | 160000 | 42.66 | 0.47

The PR also includes the fix for correctness issue reported by @davetha below.

---
Disclosure: AI (Claude Opus 5) was used to implement and test the PR.

items.title: [Perf][Kernel] Fused DSA indexer Top-k kernel (LiteTopk)
items.bodyExcerpt:
## 📌 Description

Hi @youkaichao @WoosukKwon @mgoin @hmellor @njhill @Isotr0py @DarkLight1337, could you please take a look at this PR when you have a chance?

This PR introduces two complementary SM100 prefill optimizations for DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA):

- **LiteTopK** accelerates the indexer by fusing MQA scoring, online filtering, and TopK selection without materializing the `[num_q, seq_len]` score matrix.
- **LiteDSA** further accelerates the subsequent sparse-attention computation by packing multiple neighboring queries into one larger masked attention GEMM, reusing their heavily overlapping KV sets.

To the best of our knowledge, LiteTopk is the first Indexer-Topk implementation that avoids to store the score matrix, and LiteDSA is the first that converts multiple small per-token sparse-attention GEMMs into a grouped masked GEMM while preserving each query's original attend set. The corresponding paper is available on [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11976).

**At 1M-token prefill, LiteTopK accelerates GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek-V4-Flash by 1.29× and 1.08×, respectively. LiteDSA increases the end-to-end speedups to 1.40× and 1.25×, with no accuracy loss.**

Thanks to my collaborators Jianyang Gao ([@gaoj0017](https://github.com/gaoj0017)) from ETH Zurich, Peiqi Yin ([@yinpeiqi](https://github.com/yinpeiqi)) from CUHK, and Jiangneng Li ([@gravesprite](https://github.com/gravesprite)) from NTU.

### Motivation

DSA models such as **DeepSeek-V3.2/DeepSeek-V4**, **GLM-4.6/GLM-5.2**, and **LongCat-2.0** use a sparse-attention indexer during prefill. The current indexer computes an FP8 MQA score for every query/KV pair, materializes a `[num_q, seq_len]` matrix in HBM, and then runs a per-row TopK:

items.title: [Bugfix] Count prompt-opened Poolside reasoning tokens
items.bodyExcerpt:
Count prompt-injected thinking spans through the first closing marker, including generations truncated before the marker, while preserving disabled-thinking accounting.

## Purpose

Poolside Laguna's chat template can inject the opening `<think>` token into the generation prompt. Generated token IDs then begin inside the reasoning span and contain only `</think>`, or contain no marker at all when generation is truncated.

`PoolsideV1ReasoningParser` currently inherits the default token counter through `DeepSeekV3ReasoningParser`, so the Responses API reports `reasoning_tokens=0` even when the parser emitted a reasoning item.

This change adds a Poolside-specific counter that:

- preserves zero reasoning tokens for the `IdentityReasoningParser` path;
- delegates generated `<think>...</think>` spans to the shared counter;
- counts prompt-opened reasoning up to the first `</think>`; and
- counts all generated tokens when generation truncates before `</think>`.

Fixes #49711.

This is not a duplicate of the related open PRs:

- #49743 handles output containing `</think>` without `<think>`, but its current implementation still returns zero when generation truncates before the closing marker.
- #41077 adds DeepSeek V3 forwarding and GLM-specific absent-start handling; it likewise returns zero when no closing marker is generated.
- #49728 changes Poolside's reasoning-parser enablement semantics. This change does not force reasoning on and preserves the existing Identity path for no-thinking messages and native tool calls.

The follow-up also updates ParsableContext to buffer token IDs for the current generation and count reasoning at the RequestOutput.finished boundary. This preserves streaming deltas within a generation while counting built-in-tool follow-up generations independently.

items.title: [ROCm][Perf] Skip redundant sparse index remap on non-indexer layers
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

With cross-layer index sharing, only some attention layers update the shared top-k buffer.
The old path still remapped that buffer on every layer.

This PR runs the remap only when the layer owns an indexer. For GLM-5.2 with
`index_topk_freq = 4`, this reduces remaps from 78 to 21 per forward pass.

## Safety

- Layer 0 always owns an indexer, so the shared output is initialized before reuse.
- Non-indexer layers do not change the inputs to the remap.
- The default `index_topk_freq = 1` path is unchanged.
- Speculative decoding still remaps on every layer.

## Update: indexer and non-indexer layers are two KV cache groups

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53781  added the is_index_group_leader field to MLAAttentionSpec: `is_index_group_leader=self.indexer is not None,`. Layers can only share a KV cache group if they agree on is_index_group_leader, so once the flag is set per layer, indexer and non-indexer layers land in different groups and therefore get different metadata instances with separate paged_kv_indices

```
index_group_leader_set = {spec.is_index_group_leader for spec in specs}
assert (
    ...
    and len(index_group_leader_set) == 1
    ...
), (
    "All attention layers in the same KV cache group must use the same "
    "... index-sharing role, ..."
)
```

So, remap should run for all indexer layers and the first non-indexer layer. The two non-indexer layer following the first non-indexer layer doesn't need a remap.

items.title: [ROCm][Perf] Skip cleaning sparse prefill MQA logits
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

The sparse prefill path creates the MQA-logits buffer with `torch.full(..., -inf)`.
This launches an FP32 fill before every logits kernel.

This PR passes `clean_logits=False` to AITER, so the buffer uses `torch.empty`
and the fill is removed.

## Safety

The only consumer is `top_k_per_row_prefill`. It reads each row only inside
`[cu_seqlen_ks, cu_seqlen_ke)`. Its vectorized path also guards the final partial
load, so padding values are never read. The top-k result is unchanged.

## Results

MI355X, TP=4, rank 0, comparable before/after captures:

| metric | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| FP32 fill launches | 18,162 | **0** |
| FP32 fill GPU time | 1,250.2 ms | **0 ms** |
| MQA-logits launches | 18,108 | 17,930 |

The removed fill was **0.89% of total GPU kernel time**. In the sample below it
takes 74.6 µs and is fully serialized before the logits kernel.

items.title: fix(mooncake): Restore TP replication awareness for DCP and reduce write amplification
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Motivation

When `dcp_size > 1`, `_spec_tp_replication_factor` unconditionally returns 1, forcing every TP rank to save every chunk — `tp_size`× write amplification (e.g. 8× under TP8+DCP4). This is correct but wastes store bandwidth and capacity.

### Changes

**Restore TP replication awareness** (`worker.py`):
- Remove the `if self.dcp_size > 1: return 1` override in `_spec_tp_replication_factor`, so the true factor is used (MLA=`tp_size`, GQA=`tp_size//num_kv_head`, Mamba=1).
- Generalize `put_step` to `max(1, group_put_steps[g_idx] // dcp_size)` so each chunk is saved by exactly one rank per DCP namespace, reducing write amplification from `tp_size`× to `dcp_size`×.
- Adjust `put_step_rank` to `(tp_rank // dcp_size + g_idx) % put_step` to stripe within each DCP subgroup.

**Explicit per-rank DCP namespace** (`worker.py`, `data.py`):
- Add `dcp_size`/`dcp_rank` to `KVCacheStoreSendingThread` and `KVCacheStoreRecvingThread`.
- `key_for()` gains an optional `dcp_rank` parameter; save and load pass `dcp_rank=self.dcp_rank` so each rank writes to its own namespace.
- Restructure `_init_lookup_key_prefixes` into `(shard_rank, dcp_rank, prefix)` tuples with separate TP-shard and DCP-namespace dimensions. Add `_lookup_num_shards` for the total shard count per group.

**Safety guards** (`worker.py`):
- Clamp `token_len` to `len(block_hashes) * hash_block_size` before save (prevents `AssertionError` after external cache hit).
- Skip `NULL_BLOCK_ID` chunks during load (protects against abort races).
- Early return when all load chunks are filtered out (prevents `ZeroDivisionError`).

### Performance impact (MLA, TP8, DCP4)

| Metric | main | this PR |
|--------|------|----------|
| Write amplification | 8× per chunk | 2× per chunk |
| Lookup keys per chunk | 8 | 4 |
| Correctness | ✓ | ✓ |

Deployed to GLM-5.2 (TP8, DCP4, MLA): external prefix cache hit rate 28.3%, no regressions.

items.title: [Kernel] persistent_topk: deterministic select, faster than the exact-topk workaround
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

A deterministic `persistent_topk` (the QSA / sparse-indexer block selection,
`csrc/libtorch_stable/persistent_topk.cuh`) that is **also faster than the exact-topk workaround**
people currently reach for. The kernel returns a different result for identical inputs from call to
call: the **order** always varies, and when more keys share the threshold value than the candidate
buffers hold, the selected **set** varies too. Cause: output slots are handed out by `atomicAdd` in
thread-arrival order, and exact-key ties at the last radix round are taken first-come.

### Motivation update (2026-09-21) — read this before the original framing below

This PR was opened as a determinism fix. **On the evidence since, that framing overstates the
case, and I am restating it rather than leaving the body arguing something the threads have
undermined.** Three independent readings:

1. **Ours.** We censused the top-k boundary on real traffic: **0 ties at the k-th value across 6,192
   selecting rows** at 16k context ([09-12](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55122#issuecomment-5602743511)).
   93 % of rows had fewer visible blocks than k, so selection was a no-op.
2. **The reporter of #51782.** @xueyangcs states the HPC-Ops TopK contract is **set-exact only** —
   with ties, any valid top-k set is permitted; set-stability was never guaranteed
   ([#51782, 09-09](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51782)).
3. **An independent field report.** @NNNtrance replaced the selection with an exact `torch.topk` on
   GLM-5.3-Flash across three DGX Sparks and got **9/6 bad turns vs 11/7 stock — within noise**,
   while `index_topk 8192` gives 2/3. Selection accuracy was not their cause
   ([#51782, 09-12](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51782)).

So **the tie-ordering defect is real at the kernel level but does not appear to be reachable on the
traffic that motivated it.** What survives is the performance argument, which is independently

items.title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Cap glm5next video sampling knobs
items.bodyExcerpt:
Fixes #55726

## Purpose

`glm_sample_frame_indices` walks `duration * target_fps` candidates and
deduplicates only at the end, so `Glm5NextVideoBackend` sizes that walk from the
requested fps rather than from the clip. On a 2-frame, 1-second source it spends
857 ms and 156 MiB to return 2 indices.

This clamps `target.fps` to `source.original_fps`. No sampling rate above the
source rate can return frames the container does not hold, so the walk becomes
bounded by the frame count while the sampled indices stay identical.

## Why not a fixed ceiling

An earlier revision copied GLMGA's `_MAX_FPS = 30` / `_MAX_FRAMES = 2048`. As
@JaredforReal pointed out, that ceiling has no basis in the GLM-5.3-Flash video
processor: its `processor_config.json` sets only `fps: 2` as the default
interval. A fixed 30 would also halve sampling for a legitimate 60 fps request.

Clamping to the source rate needs no magic number, and it makes the `max_frames`
ceiling unnecessary: with fps bounded, `extract_t` cannot exceed the frame count,
so `max_frames=100_000` keeps returning 10_000 indices exactly as on main.

## Measurements

Serving image, calling the backend directly, 2-frame 1-second clip, `fps` and
`max_frames` set to the same value:

| requested | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 200 000 | 11.9 ms, +1 MiB | 3.1 ms, +0 MiB |
| 2 000 000 | 87.4 ms, +18 MiB | 0.0 ms, +0 MiB |
| 20 000 000 | 857.5 ms, +156 MiB | 0.0 ms, +0 MiB |

Output is unchanged in every case: 2 indices for the 2-frame source, 900 for a

still yields the same 60 indices as the bare sampler.

items.title: WIP: fix(decode bench): remember zero-token prefix fills
items.bodyExcerpt:
DecodeBenchConnector currently records a request as filled only when the
  synthetic prefill contains at least one external token. A one-token prompt has
  a zero-token synthetic prefill, so a later preemption causes the connector to
  treat generated output as a new prompt and offer it as externally computed KV.

  With HiSparse, that false import can reach the host-only path at an arbitrary
  token offset and terminate the engine with:

  ValueError: A host-only HiSparse import must end on a cache-block boundary.

  This change records the completed one-shot lookup after allocation, even when
  the external token count is zero. This prevents generated history from being
  refilled after preemption while preserving retries after failed allocation.

  The reproduction used a two-node GLM-5.2-FP8 EP16 decode deployment with
  DecodeBenchConnector composed with HiSparseConnector, one input token, 10,624
  requested output tokens, and 128 fixed requests per GPU. The failure occurred
  when GPU KV pressure first caused requests to be preempted and readmitted.

items.title: [ROCm] Enable Hisparse on ROCm : Sparse MLA Hot-Buffering
items.bodyExcerpt:
# [ROCm] HiSparse: host-resident sparse-MLA hot-buffering on gfx950

## Purpose

Enables HiSparse (#53781) on AMD ROCm, verified on gfx950 (MI350X, CDNA4).
HiSparse keeps the bulk of the sparse-MLA KV cache in pinned host memory and
pulls back only the indexer-selected rows just in time, so long-context agentic
sessions stop getting preempted. #53781 landed it CUDA-only.

## Changes

**Route HiSparse attention through the int64-safe Triton kernel.** HiSparse
points attention at a view over the *whole multi-layer KV slab*, so emitted row
indices scale with total block count: max row index is 33 off HiSparse and 7.5M
on. AITER's decode kernel computes `row_index * row_width` in int32, so on
GLM-5.3 (`row_width=576`) it wraps above row 3,728,270 and returns approximately
zero — no NaN, no assert. Force Triton kernel for HiSparse for time being. 

**ROCm backend wiring.** CUDA HiSparse backends consume a dense `[tokens, topk]`
tensor; AITER's decode kernel consumes a ragged list plus indptr. Bridging that
is most of the diff: `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` registers with an
`index_group_builder` (which is what makes `mla_attention.py` pick up
`hisparse_cache`), decode converts dense physical top-k to ragged and attends
against the hot buffer, and prefill stages host rows via `stage_prefill_rows`
when the context is not fully resident. One new Triton kernel,
`compact_topk_to_ragged_triton` — `fetch_id_to_ragged_triton` was not reusable
because a mid-row `-1` must drop out rather than displace a valid entry.
AITER's persistent work-stealing metadata is disabled under HiSparse (its
buffers are sized in `build()`, but HiSparse rewrites the indptr at forward
time); noted as a perf follow-up.

**HIP kernel port (`csrc/`).** The four fused HiSparse cache ops build and run
on ROCm. Mechanical: vectorized copy widths, `__nv_bfloat16` → `hip_bfloat16`,
warp-primitive shims in `csrc/cuda_compat.h`. CUDA codegen unaffected.

items.title: [Bugfix] Make disable_any_whitespace actually disable whitespace on xgrammar
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`disable_any_whitespace` does not disable whitespace on the xgrammar backend — it **makes whitespace mandatory**, and as a side effect masks out the token the model wants at every JSON value position.

xgrammar's `any_whitespace=False` selects a *fixed* JSON format rather than a whitespace-free one. Its docstring is explicit that the format follows `json.dumps()` conventions, and with `separators` left unset the default is `(", ", ": ")` — *with* spaces. `backend_xgrammar.py` never passes `separators`, so today the flag requires a space after every comma and colon.

The second-order effect is the damaging one. Because the space is mandatory, the bare `"` that opens a string value becomes illegal at the value position. Measured on the mask with a real GLM-5.3 tokenizer, immediately after `{"location":`:

| grammar config | allowed tokens | whitespace-leading | bare `"` | digit-leading |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `any_whitespace=True` | 1450 | 719 | yes | 395 |
| `any_whitespace=False`, default separators — **today** | 268 | **268, all of them** | **banned** | 0 |
| `any_whitespace=False`, `separators=(",", ":")` — **this PR** | 703 | **0** | yes | 395 |

The middle row is what vLLM produces now: every legal continuation begins with a space. A model prompted for minified JSON wants the bare `"`; with it masked out, probability mass shifts to the whitespace-prefixed set, where `␣0`, `␣1`, `␣-` compete with `␣"`.

On a production GLM-5.3 deployment this corrupted **26.5%** of `response_format: {"type":"json_object"}` responses, returning a number where the first string value belonged:

```

{"location": 0.2373, "temperature": 12, ...}
{"location": 0,      "temperature": 0, ... "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"}
```

Nothing errors — `finish_reason` and `usage` are normal, so the caller simply receives wrong types.

items.title: [ROCm][Perf] Drop two dead per-step ops from the AITER sparse MLA metadata build
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`ROCMAiterMLASparseMetadataBuilder.build()` runs once per KV-cache group per scheduler step and launches two GPU ops whose results are not needed:

1. **Unused `query_lens`.** `build()` computes `query_start_loc[1:] - query_start_loc[:-1]`, but `generate_sparse_seqlen_triton` only reads its size and device; the kernel derives per-request lengths from `cu_query_lens`. The parameter is dropped and `num_seqs` is taken as `cu_query_lens.size(0) - 1`.
2. **Self-aliasing `fill_`.** `paged_kv_indptr[n + 1:].fill_(paged_kv_indptr[n])` passes a view of the tensor being filled, so ATen clones the value first. A broadcast `copy_` from the same element writes the same values without the clone.

| op | aten ops | GPU kernels |
|---|---|---|
| `x[n+1:].fill_(x[n])` | `fill_` → `clone` (`empty_strided` + copy) → `copy_` | 2 |
| `t.copy_(x[n].expand_as(t))` | `copy_` | 1 |
| `qsl[1:] - qsl[:-1]` | `sub` (+ alloc) | 1 |

Each `build()` launches two fewer kernels and makes two fewer device allocations, with no change in output. #57885 removed a similar dead op from the DSA indexer builder.

## Purpose

Fixes #58470.

NIXL P/D mis-handles a draft model's KV when **all three** hold:

1. **The target is MLA** (e.g. GLM-5.3), so NIXL maps every KV region as replicated: `total_num_kv_heads=1`, `rank_offset_factor=0`.
2. **The draft is not MLA** (e.g. DFlash2, 8 KV heads), so its KV is actually split by head across TP.
3. **Prefill TP ≠ decode TP** (e.g. a DEP8 prefill with attention TP1 feeding a TP8 decoder), so each decode rank needs a different head slice.

Drop any one and it works: an MLA draft (MTP), or equal P/D TP. `_is_region_replicated` already marks the draft regions SPLIT, but three places still use the model-wide MLA answer:

| where | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| handshake size check (`model_replicated = self.use_mla or …`) | rejects the correct geometry, accepts an unscaled draft block | checks draft regions as SPLIT |
| read offset (`_build_fa_remote`) | every decode rank reads draft head 0 | rank *r* reads head *r* |
| hetero-TP layout guard | skipped when `use_mla` | requires the same block-contiguous layout on P and D |

**Fix.** When the target is MLA and the draft isn't, build a second `TPMapping` from the draft's KV head count (`compute_tp_mapping(..., head_sharded_kv_heads=...)`). The draft's SPLIT regions use it for reads, size checks and the layout guard; MLA regions are unchanged. Prefill TP > decode TP and DCP are rejected with `NotImplementedError` for such drafts. items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

The JIT monitor is switched on after warmup, and it wraps TileLang's `JITImpl.__call__`. As a result, every TileLang kernel launch pays for the wrapper, including building the cache-miss key, even though nearly all of those calls hit the kernel cache. TileLang's `__call__` only calls `self.compile()` on a cache miss, so this PR hooks `compile` instead. The monitor still catches every post-warmup JIT compile, and cache hits no longer go through it.

This matters for models with many TileLang launches outside CUDA graphs. For example, GLM-5.3-Flash runs ~72 mhc TileLang calls per eager step (prefill / mixed batches).

**Not a duplicate:** I searched open PRs for jit_monitor / TileLang and found nothing related.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/jit_monitor/` (the fake `JITImpl` now calls `compile()` on a cache miss, like the real one).
- Microbench: 2000 `mhc_post_tilelang` calls after warmup, with the monitor off and on, on H100.
- E2E: `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, TP8 on H100, fp8 KV, MTP with 5 speculative tokens, async scheduling. Benchmark: `vllm bench serve` with random 1024 in / 128 out, each point run twice.

Unit tests: 25 passed, 7 skipped.

Microbench (µs per call):

| main (wrap `__call__`) | 15.7 | 25.9 |
| this PR (wrap `compile`) | 15.5 | 15.6 |

## Purpose

Fix two issues with multi-layer MTP on Model Runner V2 (MRV2):

1. **Multi-module MTP samples every draft step with module 0's LM head.**
   `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator` runs step `i` through MTP module `i` (`spec_step_idx=step`), but `DraftModelSpeculator.sample_draft` calls `self.model.compute_logits(hidden_states)` without `spec_step_idx`. import triton

@torch.inference_mode()
def benchmark(num_tokens: int) -> None:
    q = torch.randn(num_tokens, 16, 256, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    q_nope, q_pe = q.split([192, 64], dim=-1)
    w_uk_t = torch.randn(512, 16, 192, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16).permute(

    q_scale = torch.tensor([0.37], device="cuda")

    def prepare(ql_nope, *, fuse_projection: bool):
        return fused_q(
            positions,
            q_pe,
            rope_cache,
            index_q,
            rope_cache,
            ql_nope,

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fix two independent ways an image request takes down the engine in the GLM-5.3-Flash (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`) vision tower.

**1. Every image trips the GPU sync check.** `rot_pos_emb` builds `pos_ids` on the host and copied it with `.to(device, non_blocking=True)` from pageable memory, and the eager `forward` did the same with `cu_seqlens`. A non-blocking copy from pageable memory can block the host, so with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` the first image raises `Implicit GPU<->CPU sync detected - use a pinned, densely laid out CPU tensor, or wrap with gpu_sync_allowed()` and the engine dies.

Fix: stage `pos_ids` through pinned memory with `async_tensor_h2d`, and build the eager path's metadata with `prepare_encoder_metadata`, the same way `Glm4vVisionTransformer.forward` does (the encoder CUDA-graph path already used it). This also removes the eager-only `compute_attn_mask_seqlen`, whose GPU-side `max()` was read back with `.item()` later.

**2. Slim images overflow the vision rope table.** Since vllm-project/vllm#57387, images go through the transformers `Glm5NextImageProcessor`, whose `smart_resize` bounds them by token budget only, with no aspect-ratio cap. A slim image therefore gets a grid side beyond the hardcoded `max_position=8192`. For example, with the checkpoint's `processor_config.json`, a 200000×20 px image is accepted at 7143 tokens with `image_grid_thw = [1, 2, 14286]`, and `cos[pos_ids]` reads past the table: an `IndexError` on CPU, a device-side assert on GPU.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash cannot run with decode context parallelism. Its kpool sparse indexer compresses the indexer KV (`index_kpool=4`), and the indexer metadata builder rejects DCP whenever `compress_ratio > 1`. This check does not depend on the platform or the attention backend:

```
NotImplementedError: DCP is not supported with sparse indexer KV compression (compress_ratio=4)
```

This PR shards the kpool indexer across DCP ranks by pool:

- `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size` must be a multiple of `index_kpool` (e.g. 4), so each compressed pool lives entirely on one rank. The builder now raises a clear error when this does not hold.
- `CompressedSlotMappingKernel` is DCP-aware. Each rank writes only the compressed states it owns, at rank-local positions. Prefill chunk metadata uses the interleave measured in compressed units.
- Each rank scores its local pools, takes a local top-k, and merges it across ranks with the existing DSA DCP global top-k merge (`_merge_dcp_topk_global`), using the interleave in pool units. The result is global token ids, which the sparse MLA backend already filters and localizes under DCP.
- The CuteDSL DCP merge warmup keys use pool-level top-k and interleave for kpool models.

## Purpose

`Glm5NextMoE` constructs `FusedMoE` with `n_shared_experts=None`, so `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1` is silently ignored for GLM-5.3-Flash (`glm5_next`). Each of the 42 MoE layers keeps running the shared expert as a separate MLP (two FP8 block-scale GEMMs, the clamped SiLU and a quant) and then adds it to the routed output.

This PR wires the flag the way `DeepseekV2MoE` already does:

- `Glm5NextMoE`: when `resolve_layer_fused_shared_expert()` allows it, the separate MLP is dropped and `n_shared_experts` / `fuse_shared_experts` go to `FusedMoE`. ## Purpose

Alternative to #57169 (and its earlier version #55219). It keeps #57169's GLM-5.3-Flash move to the generic packed KV layout with a `CircularBufferSpec` tail. It replaces the builder-side re-paging of the kpool indexer with a generic, worker-side kernel-block mapping per attention group. As a result, `BlockTable` / `BlockTables` stop knowing about kernel blocks.

**Design**
- **Block tables and slot mappings** are always in KV cache manager blocks, in V1 and MRv2. `kernel_block_sizes` is removed from `BlockTable`, `MultiGroupBlockTable`, `BlockTables`, both input batches and both slot-mapping kernels. Slot values are unchanged: `b*bs + off == (b*bpk + off//kbs)*kbs + off%kbs`.
- **Mapping per attention group.** When a group's backend needs blocks smaller than the manager's (`AttentionGroup.kernel_block_size`), `AttentionGroup.build_metadata` / `build_metadata_for_cudagraph_capture` / `build_metadata_for_drafting` map its block table to kernel blocks. Kernel block `j` of block `b` is `b * kernel_block_stride + j`. The mapped table goes into a persistent per-ubatch buffer (`kernel_block_table`), so CUDA graphs see a stable address.
- **Ordinary splits.** In a dense (unpacked) layout the stride is blocks-per-kernel-block. KV views are allocated in kernel blocks as before.
- **Packed compressed caches.** Example: GLM-5.3-Flash's kpool indexer, which DeepGEMM paged MQA reads in 32/64-state pages. `AttentionGroup.map_kv_cache` re-strides the bound view over the packed blocks and takes the stride from the real tensor. items.title: [glm] [pcp] [2/n] add KCP for hybrid GLM KDA
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Enable prefill context parallelism (hybrid PCP) for GLM-5.3's KDA linear-attention layers with KCP, a two-pass parallel scan over each rank's zig-zag prefill segments on FlashKDA kernels:

1. Prepare every local segment once with FlashKDA's preparation kernel.
2. Summarize each segment as an affine map from that workspace: one FlashKDA-derived recurrence over the value columns from a zero state (S) plus the identity's columns with zero input (the transition M). Like FlashKDA's K2 after vllm-project/FlashKDA#13, it keeps the state in FP32 between tiles, and it writes BF16 `[S^T; M^T]` straight into the all-gather buffer.
3. Exchange the summaries in two parts with in-place all-gathers on a side stream, overlapping the next part's summaries and the merge.
4. Merge in chunk order in FP32 (one Triton kernel per part), reading each request's base state from the recurrent cache and writing the final state back; slots no rank has tokens in are skipped.
5. Scan with FlashKDA's K2 from the merged initial states; part-0 segments scan while part 1 is still being gathered, using K2's segment subsets.

The preparation and the scan are FlashKDA's own launches (`launch_fwd` with K1 or K2 alone); only the summary kernel is in vLLM (`csrc/flashkda_kcp.cuh`).

Plumbing:
- `PCPManager.build_hybrid_layout()` returns a model-agnostic per-step layout (decode/prefill rows, each local segment's request, zig-zag slot and token range); Mamba metadata stays on the global batch and each Mamba group binds its state slots once per step.
- The model derives its KCP plan from the layout ahead of the forward via an optional `prepare_hybrid_pcp(layout)` hook, shared by every Mamba group.
- The group coordinator gains a dim-0 in-place all-gather over power-of-two symmetric scratch per key.

items.title: [Bugfix][Executor] Size response rings for in-flight batches
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Problem

With Model Runner V2 async scheduling and a KV output aggregator, every worker rank must send a response so the aggregator can observe connector state. The multinode worker response ring is fixed at six slots, while the async pipeline can have multiple in-flight batches. A PP8 async window has nine batches, and a batch can issue both `execute_model` and `sample_tokens` RPCs before EngineCore drains the oldest future. Workers can therefore enter the full-ring polling path during normal execution.

## Change

- Size worker response rings for `2 * max_concurrent_batches` replies.
- Keep the existing ten-slot single-node floor and six-slot multinode floor.
- Thread the multinode capacity through `GroupCoordinator.create_single_reader_mq_broadcasters` as a keyword-only argument.
- Preserve all-rank replies and KV/EC output aggregation semantics.

At PP8 with async scheduling, the multinode ring grows from 6 to 18 slots. This increases the local response-ring shared-memory reservation by 48 MiB per colocated worker (24 MiB to 72 MiB at the current 4 MiB slot size). The single-node floor remains unchanged for PP sizes where the computed window is below ten.

items.title: [Rust Frontend] Share `SchemaRoot` between argument coercion and grammars
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Rust tool parsers coerce raw parameter text by the tool's JSON schema (`tool/parameters.rs`), and argument grammars (#59395) constrain the same parameters by it, but each interpreted the schema on its own. Coercion ignored `$ref`: a parameter whose schema is `{"$ref": "#/$defs/Place"}` came back as the JSON text string `"{\"city\": \"Paris\"}"` instead of an object. Pydantic v2 `model_json_schema()`, which most SDKs use to build tool schemas, emits exactly this for nested models, enums, and `Optional[Model]`:

```json
{"$defs": {"Place": {...}, "Unit": {"enum": ["celsius", "fahrenheit"], "type": "string"}},
 "properties": {"place": {"$ref": "#/$defs/Place"},
                "unit": {"$ref": "#/$defs/Unit", "default": "celsius"},
                "backup": {"anyOf": [{"$ref": "#/$defs/Place"}, {"type": "null"}], "default": null}}}
```

This affects every schema-coercing parser: Qwen Coder and MiMo, GLM, MiniMax M2/M3, Hy. DeepSeek DSML and Kimi K3 decode by their `string=`/`type=` labels instead. Coercion and grammars also disagreed on `nullable`, `const`, single-schema `allOf`, and type-name aliases such as `"int"`, so a grammar could admit a value that the parser then decodes as another type.

The open-PR search found #50933, which resolves `$ref`/`$defs` for the Python Qwen3-Coder path; there is no Rust counterpart. Python parity is not a goal here. #59190 (the Kimi K3 full-output grammar) is stacked on this PR.

  - `options` expands each reference target at most once per value, as the argument grammar walker from #59395 already did, so shared definitions cannot blow up exponentially;

items.title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Keep batch x heads out of gridDim.z in the shared FLA recurrent kernels
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

The shared FLA recurrent launchers in `vllm/third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/` put the batch x value-head product in `gridDim.z`:

```python
grid = (NK, NV, N * HV)
```

CUDA caps `gridDim.y`/`gridDim.z` at 65535, so any decode (or spec-decode) batch with `N * HV > 65535` fails to launch with `Triton Error [CUDA]: invalid argument`. For example, 1024 sequences x 64 local value heads, or 2048 x 32. This affects:

- `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_fwd`: Qwen3-Next / Qwen3.5 GDN decode, OLMo hybrid GDN
- `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update`: Qwen GDN decode / spec decode
- `fused_recurrent_kda_fwd` in `ops/kda.py`: reuses the same kernel, used by `bailing_moe_v3`

This PR flattens the grid to `grid = (N * HV * NV, NK)`, so `N * HV` lives in `gridDim.x`, whose limit is 2^31 - 1. The kernels recover `i_nh, i_v = pid // NV, pid % NV`, so the V tile varies fastest. This keeps the original launch order: the V tiles of one (sequence, head) stay adjacent and share that head's q/k/g loads in L2. The packed decode kernel in the same file already guards against this limit with `SPLIT_BATCH_HEAD_GRID`. The kernel bodies are otherwise unchanged.

A first version put `N * HV` in X and the V tiles in Y. That spread the V tiles of a head `N * HV` CTAs apart and made KDA decode up to 1.4x slower at large batches; see the benchmark below.

items.title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Pass per-sequence context lengths to the AITER paged MQA-logits kernels
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Error

MTP with native DSA-indexer decode above `next_n=2` crashes during warm-up on MI355X (seen at `next_n=3` and `next_n=6`). GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP4, `num_speculative_tokens=5` (`next_n=6`), Gluon paged MQA logits:

```
Memory access fault by GPU node-4 (Agent handle: 0x20465ea0) on address 0x792dc0bf1000. Reason: Unknown.
```

Where it does not crash, the indexer silently uses wrong causal bounds: in a direct call at `next_n=3`, the 8192-token sequence loses its last 2 valid positions in every row (9/12 rows correct).

## Cause

With native decode (`next_n > 1`), `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` receives a `(B, next_n)` table of per-row context lengths, `[b, j] = L_b - next_n + j + 1`, built in [`indexer.py#L1136-L1152`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2df122e65e87dc12870ce5f0180b49f012e7a53b/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py#L1136-L1152). The AITER Gluon `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` and `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_stage1` kernels read the table as a flat `[B]` array and some sequences get another row's length.

Example: 4 requests, `next_n=3`, context lengths 8192 / 1500 / 3000 / 700:

| `b` | `j=0` | `j=1` | `j=2` | `L_b` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 8190 | 8191 | **8192** | 8192 |
| 1 | 1498 | 1499 | **1500** | 1500 |
| 2 | 2998 | 2999 | **3000** | 3000 |
| 3 | 698 | 699 | **700** | 700 |

The kernel expects `[8192, 1500, 3000, 700]` and computes each row's bound itself. Reading the `(4, 3)` table as `[4]`, it gets the first four values in memory, `[8190, 8191, 8192, 1498]`: request 0 loses its last 2 positions in every row, and requests 1 to 3 get lengths past their own KV pages, the likely source of the fault. Column `j = next_n - 1` equals `L_b`, which is what the kernel needs.

## Fix

Pass the kernels the last column, which is the per-sequence length. `[B]` and `(B, 1)` inputs, the C4A Triton path and the torch fallback are unchanged.

items.title: [Bugfix] Keep the GLM-5.3 kpool tail and Qwen4 QSA ring out of the null block
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Block id 0 is the null block. It is shared by every KV cache group and is assumed to stay zero. Since #35431, the runners mark rows that own no state with 0 in the block table, not `PAD_SLOT_ID`: dummy runs, CUDA graph capture and padding rows all carry 0. Two ring caches that address their pages through column 0 of the block table did not treat 0 as "no ring", so dummy runs wrote their rows into block 0:

- **GLM-5.3-Flash kpool tail:** `_kpool_tail_slot_mapping_kernel` maps every token to `block_table[req][0] * kpool + pos % kpool`. Its torch fallback does the same.
- **Qwen4 QSA circular ring:** `circular_qsa_slot_mapping` and `_build_qsa_metadata_kernel` map tokens to `block_table[req, 0]` and kept every block `>= 0`. The compressed QSA path already keeps dummy slots inert (`test_qsa_compressed_metadata_keeps_dummy_slots_inert`); the ring path did not.

Every scheduled request owns its ring block, so a request on the null block has none. Its tokens now map to PAD, as the generic slot mapping does. The ring writers already skip PAD slots.

This is the same pattern as #58560, which fixes the DeepSeek-V4.1 compressor ring.

## Changes

- `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`: the kpool tail slot mapping (Triton and torch) emits PAD for requests on the null block.
- `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/common/qsa_cache.py`: the QSA circular ring slot mapping (torch and Triton) requires block `> 0`.
- Tests: the existing QSA circular metadata test, which runs the Triton builder, also checks a dummy batch (all-zero block table) and expects PAD. QSA tests that used block 0 as a real ring block now start real blocks at 1. This includes `_make_block_table` in the pre-indexer test, which could randomly hand out block 0. The kpool tail change has no new test: its unit tests run the torch fallback on CPU, while production only takes the Triton kernel. It was checked by hand on both paths.

## Overview

Structured output skipped a reasoning-end token that is also content, such as GLM's `<tool_call>` with no `</think>` before it. ## Claims

- The grammar now consumes a reasoning-end token that `ParserEngine.extract_content_ids` keeps as content, if the grammar accepts it. Close tags such as `</think>` are still skipped.
- On GLM-5.3-Flash, the doubled-`<tool_call>` signature went from 7/40 (`required`) and 8/40 (named) to 0/40 in both modes. The same holds with MTP speculative decoding: from 9/40 and 11/40 to 0/40.

## Overview

Fixes #59608. When reasoning ends on a tool-call opener instead of `</think>` (GLM-4.7/5.x can jump straight from reasoning into `<tool_call>`), the structured-output gate started the grammar constraint one token past the opener. items.bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

The Rust GLM tool parser removes leading and trailing whitespace from generated string arguments before returning them as tool calls. A tool receiving `"    return 1\n"` gets `"return 1"`. For coding agents, this can change written code or break whitespace-sensitive edit matching even when the model supplied the correct text. Preserve the original string, as the Python GLM parser already does after [#42026](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42026).

For example, an edit targeting the complete line `"    total = 1\n"` can instead match inside `subtotal = 10` once the whitespace is removed. The reproducer below shows the parser turning an intended `total = 2` edit into `subtotal = 20`.

Any model using the Rust frontend's `glm45` or `glm47` tool parser can encounter it when generated string arguments contain leading or trailing whitespace. items.bodyExcerpt:
### Summary

GLM-5.3-Flash (`glm5_next`) fails to start with any EAGLE-family drafter whose layers are plain sliding-window attention (e.g. the block-diffusion DFlash2 drafter, 5 GQA `SlidingWindowSpec` layers). `_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next` only accepts exact `MLAAttentionSpec` in the attention group, so it declines; the generic page-size unification then cannot pad the DSA indexer (MLA family) and startup dies:

```
NotImplementedError: indexer.k_cache: page size is not divisible by the maximum
page size and cannot be padded. Padding is only supported for non-MLA attention layers
```

This is the same direction as the draft-group work in #58638 (KV cache grouping for hybrid models with speculative drafters), applied to the GLM-5.3 builder, which was not covered there.

### Root cause

`_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next` builds one packed group for `MLAAttentionSpec` + indexer (MLA with `tokens_per_state > 1`) layers and aliases the kpool tails onto the indexer tensors. Its gate requires every non-Mamba / non-`KpoolTailSpec` spec to be exactly `MLAAttentionSpec`. A drafter contributes uniform `SlidingWindowSpec` layers with the draft worker's own (small) block size, so the gate returns `None`. The generic `unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size` then tries to pad every page up to the max (MLA) page; the indexer page is MLA-family and explicitly refuses padding, so `get_kv_cache_groups` raises.

### Changes

One file, `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py`:

- `_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next` splits `HiddenStateCacheSpec` (aux-eagle) and uniform drafter `SlidingWindowSpec` layers (excluding `KpoolTailSpec` / sliding-window MLA) out of `attn_specs`; the strict all-MLA gate now only applies to the target's attention layers. Absorbing the extras requires `speculative_config.use_eagle()`.

items.title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Reject cudagraph_mode=FULL at startup
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

HiSparse cannot capture prefill or mixed batches in CUDA graphs. It picks its prefill path from per-step page residency (resident pages, or spilled pages staged from host), and it mirrors prefill KV to host outside the graph. With `cudagraph_mode=FULL`, a backend reporting `ALWAYS` support (FlashInfer sparse MLA on SM100) has prefill/mixed batches captured as FULL graphs. A replay could then take the branch frozen at capture and skip the host mirror.

## Changes

HiSparse rejects `cudagraph_mode=FULL` at config validation, next to its other unsupported-config checks (PP, DCP). The error points to `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` (the default), which keeps FULL graphs for decode batches. Being a config check, it covers every backend HiSparse runs on.

Separately, `FULL` with FlashInfer sparse MLA on SM100 currently crashes on prefill replay even without HiSparse: #59681.

## Test Plan

- New `test_hisparse_rejects_full_cudagraph_mode` in `tests/test_config.py`.
- B200, shrunk GLM-5.3 (dummy weights), `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, `cudagraph_mode=FULL`, a small pool so prefill context spills to host: TRTLLM ragged and FlashAttention prefill.

## Test Result

- The new test fails without the change; `tests/test_config.py -k hisparse`: 13 passed.
- B200, before: `FULL` + HiSparse crashed in both runs: a mixed active/empty query rows error with TRTLLM ragged prefill, an illegal memory access with FlashAttention prefill. Now it fails at startup with the error above.

items.title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Expand indexer block tables when kernel blocks span several storage blocks
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Fixes the sparse-attention indexer reading the wrong cache slots on GLM-5.3-Flash/ROCm once a sequence exceeds 2048 tokens (the dense-shortcut threshold). The indexer block table is in kernel-block units (1152 tokens), but the compressed indexer cache is paged in smaller storage blocks (128 tokens). The builder only converted the table when the kernel block was *smaller* than the storage block.

## Claims

- Fixes corrupted sparse top-k selection beyond 2048 tokens for GLM-5.3-Flash on ROCm (MI355X), in both prefill and decode.
- Restores GPQA-Diamond accuracy from 80.8–85.4% (with degenerate, non-terminating generations) to 89.9–91.4%. This matches the pre-regression baseline.
- No behavior change when the kernel block size equals the storage block size or divides it (the existing path). That covers NVIDIA, DeepSeek-V3.2 and every model that doesn't set `storage_block_size`.

- `test_to_storage_block_table`: CPU-only checks of the conversion helper. It covers no kernel block size, equal sizes, kernel smaller than storage (the existing collapse) and kernel larger than storage (the new expand).
